methods.doc: method name -> {doc, params: {name: {type, required, doc}}, result: doc}

blob_header.doc: Binary data (images, audio, files) without base64. App -> host -> clients only.

client.doc: towards the host only: deliver to this client alone

coalesce.doc: true for live streams (previews): while this blob waits in a slow client's queue, a newer blob of the same stream replaces it. Default false: every blob is delivered (thumbnails, files)

meta.doc: stream-specific metadata (size, sequence, the call it answers ...)

mime.doc: media type of the data, e.g. image/jpeg

stream.doc: which stream in the app's API, e.g. `preview`, `thumb`

capabilities.attach: the app may be running before the host (started by hand) and attach to it

environment.NTWB_APP_ID: the manifest id the host launched
environment.NTWB_DATA_DIR: a writable directory for the app's own data under the host's state dir
environment.NTWB_SOCKET: path of the host's Unix socket to connect to

blob.payload: [header length u16 BE][header: UTF-8 JSON object, see BLOB_HEADER][data bytes]

json.payload: one UTF-8 JSON object: a message from MESSAGES

api.doc: path of the app's API description (see APP_API), relative to the manifest directory

description.doc: one sentence for the app list

exec.doc: argv to launch the adapter; first element absolute or relative to the manifest dir

icon.doc: path of an SVG/PNG icon, relative to the manifest directory

id.doc: unique app id; also the directory name and the URL path /apps/<id>/

single.doc: one process for all clients (default true; false is reserved)

web.doc: directory with the web UI (index.html), relative to the manifest directory

manifest.file: <data dir>/ntwb/apps/<id>/ntwb.json - searched in $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share), then each of $XDG_DATA_DIRS (default /usr/local/share:/usr/share); the first wins

bye.doc: Orderly end. From the host: the app should save and exit (it is killed after STOP_GRACE_S). From the app: it is about to exit.

call.doc: A request. The host adds `client` and forwards it to the app; the app must answer with `result` carrying the same `id`. Methods are the app's own API (its manifest `api` lists them).

client.doc: set by the host towards the app; a client never sends it

id.doc: chosen by the caller, unique among its open calls

client.close.doc: A client went away; per-client resources (subscriptions, streams) can be freed.

client.open.doc: A client attached to the app.

error.doc: The peer sent something the protocol does not allow (unknown message, bad field, unknown method...). The offending message was dropped.

about.doc: the offending message type or call id

event.doc: Something happened. To every client of the app, or to one when `client` is set.

client.doc: towards the host only: deliver to this client alone

name.doc: the event's name in the app's API

hello.doc: First message on an app connection. The host answers `welcome`, or `error` and closes.

app.doc: the app id, as in its manifest

capabilities.doc: optional features the app uses: see CAPABILITIES

ntwb.doc: protocol version the app speaks; the MAJOR must equal the host's

pid.doc: process id, for the host's process view

token.doc: NTWB_TOKEN from the environment when the host launched the app; an app started by hand may attach without one if its manifest allows `attach`

version.doc: the app's own version (shown to users)

log.doc: A line for the host's log of this app (System > Logs, `arstro-remote apps log`).

notify.doc: A request without a reply (pointer moves, slider drags). Same routing as `call`.

client.doc: set by the host towards the app

ping.doc: Liveness check; the app answers `pong` with the same `n`.

ready.doc: The app is connected. Carries the app's retained state, so a client is complete at once.

app.doc: {id, name, version} of the connected app

client.doc: this client's id (what the app sees in `call.client`)

state.doc: every retained state key -> its latest data (see `state`)

result.doc: The answer to one `call`. The host routes it to the client that made the call.

error.doc: a sentence a user understands, when not ok

ok.doc: false = the call failed; `error` says why

state.doc: Observable state. The host retains the newest `data` per `key` and replays all keys in `ready`, so a client that (re)connects is complete without asking. `data: null` deletes the key.

data.doc: the whole new value (not a delta)

key.doc: state key in the app's API

status.doc: Where the app's process is: sent on connect and on every change.

welcome.doc: The host accepted `hello`. From here on both sides may send any message of their direction.

clients.doc: clients already waiting for the app; each also gets `client.open`

roles.app: a native program with an NTWB adapter; it keeps its core and state, the host never interprets its methods
roles.client: a browser page (the app's web UI, with ntwb.js) or any other front end that speaks the WebSocket side
roles.host: Arstro Remote: registers apps, launches them, serves their web UI and relays between app and clients

types.id: string of 1-64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -
types.name: string: a lower-case letter, then up to 63 of a-z 0-9 . _ -
